subject.name: Guava
subject.scope: All 594 supplied canonical outer types, including com.google.common and Guava-owned com.google.thirdparty.publicsuffix.
subject.release_evidence: The experiment prompt identifies the selected release; no independent external release lookup was performed.

partition_kind: Inferred conceptual responsibility modules; one flat complete class partition.

evidence_summary.input_consistency: Package counts and package-edge aggregation match classes.csv and dependencies.csv.

modules.name: Core values and programming contracts
modules.responsibility: Basic values, argument checks, functional adapters, text helpers, timing, reference lifecycle support, and shared API/platform annotation declarations.

boundary_rationale.observation: The base documentation explicitly includes string utilities, function types, and other basic utilities. Preconditions and Strings depend on one another; Preconditions uses Platform, and Platform uses CharMatcher, Enums, Optional, and Strings. FinalizableReferenceQueue uses base.internal.Finalizer. The package evidence records 106 base-to-base edges and one base-to-base.internal edge. Preconditions has 312 incoming edges in the supplied class graph. All five com.google.common.annotations declarations are isolated in this graph.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep the intertwined base helpers together and assign the internal finalizer to the reference API it supports. Shared annotation declarations receive a conceptual home with programming contracts even though the graph cannot justify their ownership. Splitting text helpers from contracts would add boundaries through common checks and platform support; a separate reference-lifecycle module is not necessary at this level of explanation.

modules.name: Core collections and ordering
modules.responsibility: Ordinary maps, bimaps, lists, sets and queues; immutable implementations of those types; collection views, iteration, ordering, forwarding decorators, interning, and shared collection support.

boundary_rationale.observation: The collection documentation describes immutable support for both JDK and Guava collection types and lists iteration, ordering, forwarding, and map/set/list utilities. ImmutableMap and ImmutableBiMap depend on one another. Synchronized is used by Maps, Multimaps, Queues, Sets, and Tables; CollectCollectors is used by ordinary, multivalue, and range containers. Both collect.ForwardingBlockingDeque and util.concurrent.ForwardingBlockingDeque use collect.ForwardingDeque; util.concurrent.ForwardingBlockingQueue uses collect.ForwardingQueue.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep common collection mechanics and ordinary containers together, including the two forwarding blocking-container adapters from util.concurrent. Immutable representation is treated as a concern within each container responsibility, rather than as a module that owns all Immutable-prefixed classes. CollectCollectors, Serialization, Synchronized, and the collect annotation declarations have one home here. This is a shared conceptual core with explicit dependencies on specialized collection APIs, not an independent compilation layer.

modules.name: Multimaps and multisets
modules.responsibility: Multiple-value mappings and occurrence-counting collections, including their interfaces, mutable and immutable implementations, filtering views, sorted variants, and dedicated forwarding adapters.

boundary_rationale.observation: The documentation distinguishes Multimap and Multiset semantics. Multimap directly uses Multiset; AbstractMapBasedMultimap and ImmutableMultimap also use Multiset. ImmutableMultimap uses ImmutableMultiset as well as ordinary ImmutableList and ImmutableMap. AbstractMapBasedMultiset uses Count. TreeMultiset uses GeneralRange and BoundType.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Group multivalue maps with occurrence-counting collections because their contracts and implementations explicitly refer to one another. Keep each dedicated immutable, filtered, sorted, or forwarding implementation with its collection contract. Count belongs to the multiset implementation it serves. GeneralRange and BoundType remain in ranges, so sorted multisets have an explicit dependency on interval semantics.

modules.name: Two-dimensional tables
modules.responsibility: Row/column-keyed Table APIs, mutable and immutable representations, forwarding views, and table-specific collectors.

boundary_rationale.observation: The collection documentation defines Table by an ordered pair of keys. StandardTable uses AbstractTable, Table, and Tables; ImmutableTable uses RegularImmutableTable, SingletonImmutableTable, SparseImmutableTable, Table, TableCollectors, and Tables. The only incoming edges to TableCollectors are from ImmutableTable and Tables.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Treat row/column addressing as a distinct responsibility and keep table-specific factories and collectors with their representations. Ordinary maps, immutable collections, and synchronized views remain shared services in collections_core; their use does not turn a table implementation into an ordinary-map implementation.

modules.name: Ranges and interval collections
modules.responsibility: Range endpoints and bounds, discrete domains, contiguous sets, and range-set/range-map representations.

boundary_rationale.observation: The documentation lists Range, RangeMap, RangeSet, DiscreteDomain, and ContiguousSet as a ranges family. Range uses BoundType, Cut, and DiscreteDomain. ContiguousSet uses Range, Cut, DiscreteDomain, and its empty/regular implementations. TreeRangeMap uses Range and Cut; TreeRangeSet uses Range, RangeSet, Cut, and AbstractRangeSet. GeneralRange uses Range and BoundType, while TreeMultiset is its only incoming source in this graph.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Separate interval semantics from generic ordering and ordinary containers. Include GeneralRange with the interval vocabulary despite its current single multiset consumer; that placement is an interpretation requiring maintainer validation. Keep generic Ordering and SortedLists in the collection core. Range-based overloads and collectors create reverse references from that core, so this is a conceptual boundary with known shared implementation dependencies.

modules.name: Caching and removal policy
modules.responsibility: Cache APIs, loading, construction and configuration, eviction/removal policy, statistics, and local cache implementation support.

boundary_rationale.observation: The cache documentation identifies Cache, CacheBuilder, CacheLoader, and CacheStats. CacheBuilder uses LocalCache, LoadingCache, RemovalListener, RemovalNotification, and Weigher. LocalCache uses ReferenceEntry, RemovalCause, CacheLoader, and CacheStats. The package graph records 11 cache-to-util.concurrent edges, including LocalCache to Futures, ListenableFuture, MoreExecutors, SettableFuture, and Uninterruptibles.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep cache policy and its implementation together. Async loading depends on the execution runtime rather than requiring ownership of future classes. ReferenceEntry and counter helpers remain here because they support the cache family. The documentation discourages this API, but that status is not evidence to omit the implementation from recovery.

modules.name: Futures and execution runtime
modules.responsibility: Future values and composition, listening executors, task submission and sequencing, executor adapters, thread factories, execution exceptions, interrupt/wait helpers, and shared runtime support.

boundary_rationale.observation: The concurrency documentation names ClosingFuture, ListenableFuture, Futures, MoreExecutors, ThreadFactoryBuilder, and Uninterruptibles. Futures directly uses AbstractCatchingFuture, AbstractTransformFuture, CollectionFuture, CombinedFuture, and TimeoutFuture. MoreExecutors uses listening executor interfaces and task implementations. AbstractFuture and AbstractFutureState depend on one another. LazyLogger and Internal are referenced across futures, services, and synchronization/limit classes.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep future state machines, composition, and executor adapters in one execution responsibility. Shared LazyLogger, Internal, Platform, NullnessCasts, and Uninterruptibles have a single home here, with service/limit consumers recorded as dependencies. Unconnected local support names such as Partially receive this package-local default with low confidence; the supplied evidence cannot determine their detailed purpose.

modules.name: Service lifecycle management
modules.responsibility: Service state/lifecycle APIs, service implementation templates, service groups, and lifecycle listener dispatch.

boundary_rationale.observation: Service is named as a common concurrency type in the documentation. AbstractExecutionThreadService, AbstractIdleService, and AbstractScheduledService use AbstractService and Service. ServiceManager uses AbstractService, Service, ServiceManagerBridge, ListenerCallQueue, and Monitor. The only incoming edges to ListenerCallQueue are from AbstractService and ServiceManager.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Separate long-lived service lifecycle and listener responsibilities from task/future mechanics. Place ListenerCallQueue with its observed lifecycle consumers. Keep Monitor in synchronization_limits and executor/runtime helpers in async_execution, making their support roles visible.

modules.name: Synchronization and execution limits
modules.responsibility: Atomic state utilities, locks and monitors, striped/cycle-detecting synchronization, rate limiting, and time limits.

boundary_rationale.observation: Striped uses ForwardingCondition and ForwardingLock. RateLimiter and SmoothRateLimiter depend on one another. SimpleTimeLimiter and FakeTimeLimiter use TimeLimiter; SimpleTimeLimiter also uses UncheckedTimeoutException and Uninterruptibles. AbstractService and ServiceManager both use Monitor. Atomics is an isolated supplied class.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Group coordination primitives and execution limits as a practical responsibility rather than creating a small module for each primitive. Monitor remains a reusable synchronization concept despite its two observed lifecycle consumers. Execution exceptions, logging, Internal, and Uninterruptibles stay in the execution runtime they share; blocking collection decorators are assigned to collections_core.

modules.name: Graph models and traversal
modules.responsibility: Graph, network and value-graph APIs, builders, mutable/immutable representations, adjacency/connection machinery, and traversal.

boundary_rationale.observation: The graph documentation describes node/edge data APIs. The package graph contains 227 graph-to-graph edges. GraphBuilder uses Graph, Graphs, ImmutableGraph, MutableGraph, and StandardMutableGraph. Graphs references graph, network, and value-graph families and Traverser. Traverser uses SuccessorsFunction, BaseGraph, and Network, together with collection iterators.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep the closely related graph representations and common graph operations together. The names and relationships support one graph responsibility without enough semantic evidence to justify separate modules for each representation. Files and MoreFiles can consume traversal without moving those I/O APIs into this module.

modules.name: Hash functions and probabilistic membership
modules.responsibility: Hash functions and codes, hashers, primitive sinks/funnels, digest and checksum adapters, hashing streams, and Bloom filters.

boundary_rationale.observation: The hash documentation names hash functions and related structures. Hashing uses concrete hash implementations plus HashCode, HashFunction, and Hasher. BloomFilter uses BloomFilterStrategies and Funnel; BloomFilterStrategies uses BloomFilter, HashCode, HashFunction, and Hashing. HashingInputStream uses HashCode, HashFunction, and Hasher. The package graph contains 112 hash-to-hash edges.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep hash algorithms, their data-feeding interfaces, and Bloom-filter composition together. Hashing stream adapters remain with the hashing behavior they expose. collect.Hashing remains in collections_core because its observed consumers are collection implementations; a matching short class name is not sufficient reason to combine it with this API.

modules.name: Streams, files and resource I/O
modules.responsibility: Byte/character sources and sinks, streams and readers, file/resource operations, resource closing, line processing, and base encoding.

boundary_rationale.observation: The I/O documentation identifies ByteSource, CharSource, ByteSink, and CharSink as its core. ByteSource uses ByteSink, ByteStreams, CharSource, Closer, MultiInputStream, and BaseEncoding. BaseEncoding uses all four source/sink types. Files and MoreFiles each use graph.SuccessorsFunction and graph.Traverser; ByteSource and Files also use hash APIs.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep stream acquisition, processing, closing, and file/resource integration together. BaseEncoding stays with its source/sink integration. Traversal and hashing are supporting dependencies, not reasons to dissolve the I/O responsibility.

modules.name: Primitive value utilities
modules.responsibility: Primitive-type utilities and conversions, unsigned value types, immutable primitive arrays, and associated platform helpers.

boundary_rationale.observation: The primitive documentation explicitly describes utilities for primitive types plus unsigned values and immutable arrays. The graph has five math-to-primitives edges: IntMath to Ints, LongMath to UnsignedLongs, PairedStatsAccumulator to Doubles, and Quantiles to Doubles and Ints. There are no primitives-to-math edges in the supplied graph.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Separate representation, conversion, and primitive storage from mathematical algorithms. Keep immutable primitive arrays with primitive values rather than placing every immutable type in the object collection modules. The observed direction supports this conceptual distinction without proving an intended layering rule.

modules.name: Arithmetic and statistics
modules.responsibility: Arithmetic and rounding over numeric values, quantiles, statistical summaries/accumulators, and linear transformations.

boundary_rationale.observation: The math documentation describes arithmetic over primitives, BigInteger, and BigDecimal. StatsAccumulator uses DoubleUtils and Stats. PairedStatsAccumulator uses LinearTransformation, PairedStats, Stats, StatsAccumulator, and primitives.Doubles. The inventory includes quantiles and rounding helpers as well as arithmetic classes.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Treat numeric computation as a responsibility distinct from primitive representation. Keep statistics and arithmetic in one modest-sized module; the evidence does not require separate numerical submodules.

modules.name: Network identifiers and protocol values
modules.responsibility: IP addresses, host/port specifications, domain names and owned public-suffix support, media types, and HTTP constants.

boundary_rationale.observation: The networking documentation mentions IP addresses and domain names. InternetDomainName directly uses PublicSuffixPatterns, PublicSuffixTrie, and PublicSuffixType, accounting for all three net-to-publicsuffix edges. PublicSuffixPatterns uses PublicSuffixTrie; PublicSuffixTrie uses PublicSuffixType. MediaType uses collection and base APIs. HttpHeaders and net.ParametricNullness are isolated.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Include all three Guava-owned public-suffix types with domain-name functionality despite their thirdparty namespace. Exclude PercentEscaper and UrlEscapers from this conceptual responsibility because they implement escaping. Preserve HttpHeaders and the local annotation with the network family based on semantic/package evidence, not on inferred graph importance.

modules.name: Text escaping policies
modules.responsibility: Generic character/Unicode escape abstractions, escaper builders, and HTML, XML, and URL escaping policies.

boundary_rationale.observation: The escape package documentation explicitly names HtmlEscapers, XmlEscapers, and UrlEscapers as additional implementations. HtmlEscapers and XmlEscapers each use Escaper and Escapers. PercentEscaper uses UnicodeEscaper; UrlEscapers uses Escaper and PercentEscaper. These give six html/xml/net-to-escape edges in the package graph.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Create one escaping responsibility across escape, html, xml, and the two URL-related net classes. The html/xml annotation declarations follow their local escaping implementations. General base text manipulation stays in foundation and BaseEncoding stays in io_resources because their observed relationships support different responsibilities.

modules.name: Reflection and generic types
modules.responsibility: Generic type capture/resolution, type tokens, invocation and parameter inspection, type-to-instance maps, class-path inspection, and reflection helpers.

boundary_rationale.observation: The reflection documentation identifies the package as reflection utilities. TypeToken uses Invokable, TypeCapture, TypeParameter, TypeResolver, TypeVisitor, and Types. TypeResolver uses TypeVisitor and Types. ClassPath has the three reflect-to-io edges: to ByteSource, CharSource, and Resources. The collect documentation instead lists ClassToInstanceMap among collection types.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep reflective type reasoning and discovery together, including ClassPath as a consumer of I/O. Leave raw ClassToInstanceMap implementations in collections_core and generic TypeToInstanceMap implementations here; the documentation and local type-resolution relationships are stronger evidence than similar map suffixes alone.

modules.name: Event subscription and dispatch
modules.responsibility: Event bus APIs, synchronous/asynchronous dispatch support, subscription declarations, subscriber discovery, and exception handling.

boundary_rationale.observation: The eventbus documentation describes publish-subscribe communication. EventBus uses Dispatcher, SubscriberRegistry, DeadEvent, and subscriber exception interfaces. SubscriberRegistry uses cache.CacheBuilder, CacheLoader, and LoadingCache, plus reflect.TypeToken. Subscribe and AllowConcurrentEvents are isolated annotation declarations because annotation applications are absent from the graph.
boundary_rationale.interpretation: Keep dispatch behavior, subscription semantics, and subscriber discovery together. Caching and reflection are collaborators used by subscriber discovery, not parts to duplicate into the event module. Retain subscription annotations despite the missing annotation-use edges. The documentation discourages the API, but the recovery must still account for its supplied classes.

cross_module_observations.observation: Preconditions has 312 incoming directed class edges. Package dependency counts include 184 collect-to-base, 67 util.concurrent-to-base, and 45 graph-to-base edges. The supplied base edges remain within base and base.internal.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: The foundation is a shared dependency provider. Frequent use justifies making it visible to readers; it does not mean consumers should be merged into it or that invocation frequency has been measured.

cross_module_observations.observation: Maps and Sets use Range and BoundType; CollectCollectors uses ImmutableRangeMap and ImmutableRangeSet. Range and interval containers use Ordering and ordinary immutable collections. ImmutableMap uses ImmutableSetMultimap, and ImmutableMultimap uses ImmutableMap. Synchronized refers to Table, Multimap, and Multiset, while their utilities use Synchronized.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: The collection partition has dependencies in both directions between core and specialized responsibilities. It describes conceptual ownership, not a validated acyclic dependency layer or immediately extractable Java module layout. Shared helpers are assigned once.

cross_module_observations.observation: The package graph has 11 cache-to-util.concurrent edges. LocalCache uses Futures, ListenableFuture, MoreExecutors, SettableFuture, and Uninterruptibles. SubscriberRegistry accounts for all three eventbus-to-cache edges and the eventbus-to-reflect TypeToken edge.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: Caching and event dispatch are composite facilities built on execution/type services; their collaborators remain in their own responsibilities.

cross_module_observations.observation: AbstractService and ServiceManager are the only incoming sources for ListenerCallQueue and Monitor. ListenerCallQueue uses LazyLogger; service templates use MoreExecutors and Platform. RateLimiter and SimpleTimeLimiter use Uninterruptibles.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: ListenerCallQueue is placed with lifecycle behavior, Monitor with coordination, and shared runtime helpers with execution. The distinction between dedicated listener machinery and reusable coordination concepts is semantic and requires maintainer review.

cross_module_observations.observation: HtmlEscapers and XmlEscapers each use Escaper and Escapers; PercentEscaper uses UnicodeEscaper; UrlEscapers uses Escaper and PercentEscaper. The package documentation explicitly connects these families.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: Combining these classes expresses a cross-package escaping responsibility supported by both documentation and concrete relationships.

cross_module_observations.observation: InternetDomainName uses each of the three supplied com.google.thirdparty.publicsuffix types. PublicSuffixPatterns uses PublicSuffixTrie, which uses PublicSuffixType.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: The owned suffix implementation belongs conceptually with domain-name interpretation, not an out-of-scope external dependency or a standalone third-party module.

cross_module_observations.observation: Files and MoreFiles each use graph.Traverser and graph.SuccessorsFunction, giving four io-to-graph edges. The graph records seven io-to-hash edges. ClassPath uses ByteSource, CharSource, and Resources, giving three reflect-to-io edges.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: Higher-level facilities compose traversal, hashing, and stream services. Those uses explain dependencies while preserving the responsibility of the consuming API.

cross_module_observations.observation: There are five math-to-primitives edges and zero primitives-to-math edges in the supplied package graph. Documentation distinguishes numeric algorithms from primitive utilities, unsigned values, and immutable primitive arrays.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: Primitive representation and mathematical computation are distinct conceptual responsibilities; the direction is release-specific evidence rather than a claimed universal design rule.

cross_module_observations.observation: The inventory contains 45 vertices with no incoming or outgoing supplied edge: all 31 annotation declarations and 14 other types. Examples include base.Charsets, io.Flushables, net.HttpHeaders, reflect.AbstractInvocationHandler, and util.concurrent.Atomics.
cross_module_observations.interpretation: Isolation in this restricted graph is not evidence of dead code, lack of API use, or low architectural importance. Names/documentation/package context provide the only available basis for these placements.

changes_from_initial_hypothesis.initial_hypothesis: One broad collection area with possible subareas.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.final_decision: Four responsibilities: collections_core, multimaps_multisets, tables, and ranges.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.evidence_and_reason: Documentation names multiple collection contracts and range semantics; direct references between Multimap and Multiset support their joint family, while table-specific implementations and collectors support a separate Table responsibility. Shared helpers and immutable representations prevent interpreting the split as clean compilation layers.

changes_from_initial_hypothesis.initial_hypothesis: One broad concurrency area with candidate lifecycle/coordination subdivisions.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.final_decision: async_execution, service_lifecycle, and synchronization_limits; two blocking forwarding adapters join collections_core.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.evidence_and_reason: Futures and executor composition share direct implementation relationships; lifecycle templates and ListenerCallQueue form a recognizable responsibility; atomic/lock/rate/time APIs express coordination. The two forwarding adapters directly reuse core collection forwarding types.

changes_from_initial_hypothesis.initial_hypothesis: Primitive values and numerical methods provisionally grouped.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.evidence_and_reason: Documentation distinguishes representation/storage from arithmetic, and all five observed math/primitives cross-package edges point toward primitive utilities.

changes_from_initial_hypothesis.initial_hypothesis: Possible separation or combination of base text helpers with other text concerns.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.final_decision: Keep the base family in foundation; create text_escaping only for escape abstractions and HTML/XML/URL policies.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.evidence_and_reason: Preconditions, Strings, and Platform have direct reciprocal relationships, while escape documentation explicitly identifies the HTML/XML/URL implementations.

changes_from_initial_hypothesis.initial_hypothesis: Public-suffix support may belong with domain-name handling.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.final_decision: All three publicsuffix classes join network_values.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.evidence_and_reason: InternetDomainName directly uses all three types, and those implementation types reference one another.

changes_from_initial_hypothesis.initial_hypothesis: Caching, graphs, hashing, I/O, reflection, and event dispatch as independent responsibilities.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.final_decision: Retain those responsibility areas while documenting their dependencies.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.evidence_and_reason: The package summaries and class relationships confirm recognizable responsibilities; external uses of their APIs do not justify duplicating or absorbing their classes into consuming modules.

changes_from_initial_hypothesis.initial_hypothesis: Preserve isolated and annotation types with their supported families.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.final_decision: All 45 isolated vertices are assigned; local ambiguous declarations follow a stated conceptual default.
changes_from_initial_hypothesis.evidence_and_reason: All 31 annotation declarations are isolated because annotation applications are absent. The dependency graph cannot resolve their detailed ownership.

limitations: This is an inferred conceptual partition for the supplied 33.7.2 JRE evidence. No maintainer-validated intended architecture or architectural ground truth was supplied, and no claim of architectural accuracy or superiority is made.

Only the five permitted evidence files and the experiment prompt were read. No source class implementations, baseline partitions, UE decisions, reports, numeric quality scores, or external sources were inspected.

Package names and documentation seeded the vocabulary and remain a substantial bias. Several final modules preserve packages, and ambiguous support/annotation types default to the relevant package family. Cross-package groups and package splits reduce but do not remove this bias.

The binary, unweighted, directed internal graph records supplied type/member-use relationships, not execution frequency, calls at runtime, change history, team ownership, design intent, or public API demand.

Inner and anonymous classes are merged into outer types, external libraries are excluded, and annotation applications are not edges. Reflection, dynamic registration, resource dependencies, and build-time constraints may be absent or underrepresented.
All 31 annotation declarations and 14 other types are isolated. Their assignments rely on names and available package context, not positive graph evidence. Missing edges do not establish dead code.
The supplied package documentation has no section for base.internal or com.google.thirdparty.publicsuffix. Their inclusion and placement rely on the inventory and class relationships.

Collection support types such as CollectCollectors, Serialization, and Synchronized span conceptual responsibilities. The final collection modules have dependencies in both directions; package-private access, visibility, compatibility, and physical extraction feasibility were not examined.

GeneralRange in ranges, Monitor in synchronization_limits, ambiguous execution support in async_execution, and shared annotations in foundation are semantic choices requiring maintainer validation. The 18-module granularity is a practical reviewer choice, not an inferred official module count.
No MQ, cohesion, coupling, or other architecture quality score was computed or optimized, and there was no comparison with baseline algorithms. Raw graph counts describe observations only.
